cause: Two registers or clusters at the same level of a peripheral or cluster end up with the same display name. svdconv compares each register's <displayName> and, where a register has none (and for clusters, which have no <displayName>), its <name>; so registers that share a <name> in different <alternateGroup>s collide here even though the name check accepts them.
fix: Give each register at that level a unique <displayName>, or drop a copied <displayName> so the distinct <name> is used. For registers with the same <name> in different <alternateGroup>s, add a distinct <displayName> to each, e.g. <displayName>CTRL_ALT</displayName>. The line in the message points to the first definition.
note: Error under --strict. The name check appends <alternateGroup> to the name (SvdPeripheral.cpp:806-809) but the displayName check does not, so equal names in different alternate groups without explicit <displayName> look like a false positive.

cause: A <field> has more than two <enumeratedValues> containers. svdconv allows one container (usage read, write or read-write) or two (one read, one write); the third and later containers are ignored, and M374 follows with the rule.
fix: Merge the extra <enumeratedValues> into the existing ones so the field keeps at most two: one container for all values, or one with <usage>read</usage> and one with <usage>write</usage>.
note: CMSIS-SVD.xsd 1.3.9 also limits <enumeratedValues> to maxOccurs=2 in fieldType.

cause: A <field> has two <enumeratedValues> containers with the same usage. A container without <usage> counts as read-write, so two containers that both omit <usage>, or both say read (or both write), collide; the second one is ignored.
fix: Merge the two containers into one, or set <usage>read</usage> on one and <usage>write</usage> on the other.

cause: A <field> has a read-write <enumeratedValues> container (explicit <usage>read-write</usage> or no <usage>) together with a read or a write container. The read-write container already covers both directions, so the read or write container is ignored.
fix: Keep a single container for all values, or split them into exactly one <usage>read</usage> and one <usage>write</usage> container; add the missing <usage> to the container that has none.

cause: A register array (a <register> with <dim> and a <name> ending in [%s]) has a <dimIncrement> that is not exactly its size in bytes: svdconv requires dimIncrement*8 to equal the register <size> in bits, because the array is generated as a contiguous C array; the register is dropped. svdconv also raises M378 for a <peripheral> whose <baseAddress> is missing or unparsable, and the text then still speaks of a register array.
fix: Make <dimIncrement> equal to the register size in bytes, e.g. <size>32</size> with <dimIncrement>4</dimIncrement>. If the registers are spaced further apart, use a %s list instead (<name>CH%s</name>) or put the register into a <cluster> array that carries the larger <dimIncrement>. If NAME is a peripheral, give it a valid <baseAddress>.
note: Misleading reuse: SvdPeripheral.cpp:1502 logs M378 (register-array text, NUM/NUM2 unset) for a peripheral without a valid <baseAddress>. M366 is the related check that the increment is not smaller than the register.

cause: An <enumeratedValue> <value> uses binary don't-care notation (0b... or #... with x digits) with more than 8 'x' characters. svdconv expands every x into all combinations and refuses more than 8 (256 values), so the value is rejected with M202 and the enumeratedValue is dropped.
fix: Use at most 8 x digits in one <value>: split it into several <enumeratedValue>s, or cover the remaining values with one <enumeratedValue> that has <isDefault>true</isDefault> instead of a <value>.
note: Logged without a line number; the M202 for <value> that follows carries it. Error under --strict.

cause: An <addressBlock> of a peripheral ends beyond 0xFFFFFFFF: the peripheral <baseAddress> plus the block's <offset> and <size> - 1 does not fit into 32 bits. svdconv ignores that address block.
fix: Correct the peripheral's <baseAddress> or the address block's <offset> and <size> so the block ends at or below 0xFFFFFFFF; <size> is the length of the block, not its end address.
note: Error under --strict. TEXT prints the range as [end ... start]; ADDR is cast to 32 bits.

cause: An <interrupt> <value> is greater than or equal to <cpu><deviceNumInterrupts>. Valid numbers run from 0 to deviceNumInterrupts-1, so the interrupt is dropped.
fix: Correct the interrupt's <value>, or raise <deviceNumInterrupts> to the highest interrupt number plus one.

cause: A register's <resetValue> or <resetMask> has bits set above the register width (e.g. 0x1FF for an 8-bit register); the width is the register's effective <size>, which may be inherited from the peripheral or device. svdconv replaces the value with 0.
fix: Make <resetValue> and <resetMask> fit the register width, e.g. <resetMask>0xFF</resetMask> for <size>8</size>, or correct the register's <size> if that is what is wrong.
note: Error under --strict. NAME2 says which of the two values failed (Reset Value or Reset Mask).

cause: <cpu> sets <pmuNumEventCnt> but <pmuPresent> is missing or false, so the counter number has nothing to apply to.
fix: Add <pmuPresent>true</pmuPresent> to <cpu> if the core has a PMU, or remove <pmuNumEventCnt>.
note: pmuPresent and pmuNumEventCnt are parsed by svdconv (SvdCpu.cpp:203-215) but are not in the CMSIS-SVD.xsd 1.3.9 shipped with CMSIS 5.9.0; they belong to a later schema version. The message has no line number.

cause: <cpu> has <pmuPresent>true</pmuPresent> for a core that has a PMU, but <pmuNumEventCnt> is missing or outside the accepted range. svdconv then ignores the PMU entry.
fix: Add <pmuNumEventCnt> with the number of PMU event counters of the core, a value from 2 to 31, e.g. <pmuNumEventCnt>8</pmuNumEventCnt>.
note: The message says [2..31] but the check rejects only <2 or >32, so 32 passes (SvdCpu.cpp:368). pmuPresent and pmuNumEventCnt are parsed by svdconv but are not in the CMSIS-SVD.xsd 1.3.9 of CMSIS 5.9.0.

cause: <cpu> sets <pmuPresent>true</pmuPresent> but the core named in <cpu><name> has no PMU in svdconv's CPU table; only CM52, CM55, CM85, ARMV81MML, SMC2 and SMC3 have one. svdconv drops the PMU setting.
fix: Remove <pmuPresent> and <pmuNumEventCnt> for this core, or correct <cpu><name> if the device really uses a core with a PMU (e.g. CM55 or CM85).
note: No line number in the message. pmuPresent and pmuNumEventCnt are parsed by svdconv but are not in the CMSIS-SVD.xsd 1.3.9 of CMSIS 5.9.0.

cause: A <name> contains square brackets other than a trailing [%s] on a dim element, e.g. <name>Data[0]</name> on a register without <dim>. Brackets are not valid in a C identifier, so svdconv drops the element.
fix: Remove the brackets (<name>Data0</name>), or describe the element as an array: <name>Data[%s]</name> with <dim> and <dimIncrement>.

cause: <cpu> contains a <sauRegionsConfig> but <sauNumRegions> is 0. svdconv ignores the SAU region configuration.
fix: Set <sauNumRegions> to the number of SAU regions the device implements (at least the number of <region> entries), or remove <sauRegionsConfig> if the device has no SAU.

cause: <cpu> sets <mveFP> to true while <mvePresent> is missing or false; MVE floating point requires MVE.
fix: Add <mvePresent>true</mvePresent> to <cpu> when the core implements MVE with floating point, or set <mveFP> to false (or remove it) for an integer-only or no-MVE configuration.
note: Dead check at 30f5e81: the test (m_mveFP && !m_mvePresent) sits inside if(m_mvePresent), so svdconv never reports M388. mvePresent and mveFP are not in the CMSIS-SVD.xsd 1.3.9 of CMSIS 5.9.0.

cause: <cpu><deviceNumInterrupts> is larger than the maximum number of external interrupts of the core named in <cpu><name> (svdconv's table: 32 for CM0/CM0PLUS/CM1, 240 for CM3/CM4/CM7/CM23, 480 for CM33/CM55/CM85). svdconv reports it for every <interrupt> and drops each of them.
fix: Set <deviceNumInterrupts> to the real number of device interrupts, which cannot exceed the core's limit, or correct <cpu><name> if the wrong core is named.
note: Message says 'greater or equal' but the check is strictly greater; a value equal to the limit passes (SvdInterruptTest.cpp:112-116). The line number is that of each interrupt, not of <cpu>.

cause: <cpu><sauRegionsConfig> lists more <region> entries than <sauNumRegions> allows.
fix: Raise <sauNumRegions> to the number of SAU regions the device has, or remove the surplus <region> entries.

cause: During SFD generation (--generate=sfd or sfr) a text contains a character svdconv cannot write into the SFD file: a byte outside printable ASCII 0x20..0x7E (UTF-8 letters, µ, ©, typographic quotes or dashes, each byte reported separately) or a double quote. The description of a peripheral, cluster, register, field, interrupt or enumerated value is checked, falling back to its displayName or name; non-ASCII bytes are dropped and double quotes escaped.
fix: Replace the character in the <description> (or <displayName>/<name> when there is no description) with plain ASCII, e.g. 'u' or 'micro' for µ, ' instead of typographic quotes, - instead of an en dash, and avoid double quotes.
note: Called without a line number (default -1). The same text usually raised M216 in the check phase.

cause: During SFD generation a description contains two question marks followed by another character ('??x'), which a C preprocessor could read as a trigraph. svdconv reports any character after '??', not only the nine trigraph characters, and drops that character.
fix: Remove or reword the '??' in the <description>, e.g. write a single '?' or '(unknown)'.

cause: During SFD generation a description contains a backslash followed by a character other than 'n' (e.g. \t, \r, \\ or a Windows path). Only \n is supported; svdconv drops the character after the backslash.
fix: Remove the backslash or rewrite the text: use \n for a line break, write paths with '/', and use no other C escape sequences in <description>.
note: Source FIXME (SvdUtils.cpp:1310) notes the conversion mangles such sequences.

Not raised anywhere in svdconv at 30f5e81: the code appears only in the message table (SVDConv_Msgs.cpp:38) and the README (README.md:219). Unexpected exceptions are reported as M104 ('STL exception occurred: ...' or 'Unknown exception occurred!') instead.
Not raised anywhere in svdconv at 30f5e81: the code appears only in the message table (SVDConv_Msgs.cpp:39) and the README (README.md:220).

cause: An internal consistency check of svdconv failed; REF names the check. In this version it is raised only while generating the C expression of a <disableCondition>, when an item referenced at field level is not a field.
fix: Check that every name in the <disableCondition> refers to an existing register or field. If the SVD is correct, report the message together with the SVD file to Open-CMSIS-Pack/devtools.
note: Only call site SvdCExpression.cpp:179; how an SVD reaches it is not evident from the code.

Not raised anywhere in svdconv at 30f5e81: the code appears only in the message table (SVDConv_Msgs.cpp:44) and the README (README.md:225). A file that is not well-formed XML ends in M111 'Reading SVD File failed!' (SVDConv.cpp:213-218).

cause: With --generate=sfr on Windows, svdconv looks for SfrCC2.exe in the directory of svdconv.exe and did not find it at the path shown. This is the only place svdconv raises M109.
fix: Put SfrCC2.exe (from Keil MDK/uVision) into the same directory as svdconv.exe, or generate --generate=sfd instead, which needs no SfrCC2.

cause: svdconv rejected its command line.
fix: Call svdconv with one SVD file and supported options only; svdconv -h lists them (-o/--outdir, --generate=header|partition|sfd|sfr|peripheralMap|registerMap|fieldMap, --fields=struct|struct-ansic|macro|enum, --strict, -b/--log, -x/--diag-suppress, --create-folder, ...).
note: Not raised anywhere in svdconv at 30f5e81: the code appears only in the message table (SVDConv_Msgs.cpp:50) and the README (README.md:229). Option errors are printed by cxxopts as '<program> error: <text>' and svdconv exits with 1, although the README return-code table says 3.

cause: An '@', which introduces a command file of options, was given on the svdconv command line without a file name after it.
fix: Put the command file name after '@' (e.g. @options.txt) or pass the options directly on the command line.
note: Not raised anywhere in svdconv at 30f5e81: the code appears only in the message table (SVDConv_Msgs.cpp:52) and the README (README.md:231). The cxxopts parser in this version has no '@' command-file handling.

cause: A path given on the command line does not exist: the input SVD file, or the output directory of -o/--outdir when --create-folder is not given. Relative paths are resolved against the current working directory.
fix: Correct the path of the .svd file or of the -o directory, or add --create-folder so svdconv creates the output directory.

cause: With --generate=sfr on Windows, svdconv could not start SfrCC2.exe (opening the pipe to the command failed); PATH shows the command it tried.
fix: Check that SfrCC2.exe exists next to svdconv.exe and can be started from a command prompt; otherwise use --generate=sfd.

cause: With --generate=sfr, SfrCC2.exe compiled the generated .sfd file and exited with code 2 or higher, i.e. it found errors. Its own output is printed just before, in the M125 'SfrCC2 report' block.
fix: Read the SfrCC2 report (M125) printed before this message, correct the SVD element that produced the reported .sfd line, and regenerate.

cause: With --generate=sfr, SfrCC2.exe compiled the generated .sfd file and exited with code 1, i.e. it reported warnings. Its own output is printed just before, in the M125 'SfrCC2 report' block.
fix: Read the SfrCC2 report (M125) printed before this message and correct the SVD elements it points to; the .sfr file is still produced.

cause: An option on the svdconv command line is not known.
fix: Check the option against svdconv -h and correct its spelling.
note: Not raised anywhere in svdconv at 30f5e81: the code appears only in the message table (SVDConv_Msgs.cpp:59) and the README (README.md:238). Unknown options make cxxopts print '<program> error: ...' (exit 1); unknown values of --generate, --fields and --debug are silently ignored.

cause: svdconv could not open an output file (header, partition, SFD or listing) for writing. The file name is built from the output directory and <device><name>; the directory is not writable, an existing file is read-only or locked, or the name is not a valid file name.
fix: Choose a writable output directory with -o, close programs that hold the file open, remove a read-only attribute, and check that <device><name> contains only characters valid in file names.

cause: --generate=sfr was used on Linux or macOS. SFR generation runs SfrCC2.exe, which exists only on Windows, so svdconv stops after the intermediate .sfd file and exits with code 2.
fix: Use --generate=sfd on Linux and macOS, or run --generate=sfr on Windows with SfrCC2.exe (from Keil MDK/uVision) in the same directory as svdconv.exe.

cause: An element is misspelled or placed under a parent that does not accept it, e.g. <headerStructName> inside a <register>, or <protection> inside a <field> or <interrupt>. svdconv ignores the element; only the first 10 unknown tags of a run are reported.
fix: Check the tag spelling (names are case-sensitive) and move the element to a level where CMSIS-SVD.xsd allows it, or delete it. Vendor-specific data belongs in <vendorExtensions> at the end of <device>.
note: The 10-message limit is a static counter (SvdItem.cpp:210, 260); misplaced <protection> is always reported. Tags containing 'dim' are routed to the dim check and give M240 instead.

cause: svdconv cannot convert the element's value: a number that is not plain decimal, 0x hex or 0b/# binary, a boolean other than true/false/1/0, or a token outside the allowed list (e.g. <usage>, <endian>, <modifiedWriteValues>, <readAction>, <protection>). A leading '+' and the k/M/G/T scale suffix are rejected although the CMSIS-SVD schema pattern allows them.
fix: Write the value in a form svdconv parses: decimal (4096), hex (0x1000) or binary (0b1010) numbers, true or false for flags, and the exact schema token for enumerated values. Replace scaled values such as 4k with 0x1000.
note: Empty values give M205 and <access> values give M233 instead. scaledNonNegativeInteger in CMSIS-SVD.xsd 1.3.9 is '[+]?(0x|0X|#)?[0-9a-fA-F]+[kmgtKMGT]?'.

cause: In this svdconv version it is raised only for the derivedFrom attribute: an element receives a derivedFrom reference while it already has one. An XML element cannot carry the attribute twice, so a well-formed SVD file should not produce it.
fix: Keep a single derivedFrom attribute on the element at the reported line; if the message persists, report it with the SVD file to Open-CMSIS-Pack/devtools.
note: Attributes are stored in a std::map and processed once per element, so the condition looks unreachable from a file.

cause: <cpu><revision> is not of the form rNpM with N and M from 0 to 255 (e.g. r0p1). svdconv also reports M325 because no valid revision is set.
fix: Write the core revision as rNpM (N = major, M = minor revision), for example <revision>r1p0</revision>.
note: SvdDimension.cpp:360-363, 393-395 and 425-427 also log M204 for an invalid name/displayName/description expression, but the parser never returns that result at this commit.

cause: An element whose value svdconv converts (a number, boolean, access, usage or other token, an enumeratedValue <value>) is present but empty, e.g. <resetValue></resetValue> or <access/>. The element is treated as not set.
fix: Give the element a value, or remove it so the inherited or default value applies.

cause: The derivedFrom attribute names an element svdconv cannot find. The source must be of the same kind (peripheral from peripheral, register from register, ...), must appear earlier in the file because derivedFrom is resolved while parsing, and is looked up among the siblings first and otherwise by a dotted path from the peripheral level (PERIPH.REG). The deriving element is dropped.
fix: Correct the spelling (case-sensitive) of the derivedFrom value, move the source element above the deriving one, and use the dotted path (e.g. derivedFrom="TIMER0.CR1") when the source lies in another peripheral or register.
note: NAME is printed with '%' characters removed. For a <dim> source the lookup compares the <name> as written, including %s or [%s] (SvdItem.cpp:450-463).

cause: An element without <dim> has %s or a trailing [%s] in its <name>, <displayName> or <description>. These placeholders are expanded only for dim elements, so svdconv drops the element; a literal '%s' in a description triggers it too. NAME shows the text with the placeholder removed.
fix: Add <dim> and <dimIncrement> (and <dimIndex> for a %s list) if the element is meant to repeat; otherwise remove %s / [%s] from the name, displayName and description.

cause: A dim element uses the array form [%s] in its <name> and also has <dimIndex>. Arrays are always indexed 0..dim-1, so svdconv ignores the <dimIndex>.
fix: Remove <dimIndex>, or, if the custom indices are wanted, switch to the list form with %s (e.g. <name>CH%s</name>), which creates separate elements named with the <dimIndex> values.
note: Error under --strict. Not raised for elements that got the dim data through derivedFrom.

cause: The <device> has no <cpu> element. svdconv needs it for the core configuration in the CMSIS header and for the interrupt checks, and debuggers use it; header generation reports M209 again.
fix: Add a <cpu> element to <device> (after <description>/<licenseText>) with the values of the actual core, e.g. <cpu><name>CM4</name><revision>r0p1</revision><endian>little</endian><mpuPresent>true</mpuPresent><fpuPresent>true</fpuPresent><nvicPrioBits>4</nvicPrioBits><vendorSystickConfig>false</vendorSystickConfig></cpu>.

cause: The <device> has schemaVersion="1.0" and no <cpu> element; CMSIS-SVD 1.0 had no <cpu> section.
fix: Set schemaVersion on <device> to 1.1 or later (e.g. schemaVersion="1.3") and add a <cpu> element for the core, e.g. <cpu><name>CM4</name><revision>r0p1</revision><endian>little</endian><mpuPresent>true</mpuPresent><fpuPresent>true</fpuPresent><nvicPrioBits>4</nvicPrioBits><vendorSystickConfig>false</vendorSystickConfig></cpu>.

cause: An <addressBlock> <usage> is not one of registers, buffer or reserved. svdconv also reports M202 for that line and leaves the usage unset.
fix: Use <usage>registers</usage>, <usage>buffer</usage> or <usage>reserved</usage> in each <addressBlock>.
note: M212 carries no line number; the M202 that follows does.

cause: An element has dim data but lacks <dim> or <dimIncrement>; both are required as soon as any dim element (<dim>, <dimIncrement>, <dimIndex>, <dimName>) is present. svdconv drops the element.
fix: Add the missing element, e.g. <dim>4</dim> and <dimIncrement>0x4</dimIncrement>, or remove the other dim elements if the element does not repeat.

cause: A <peripheral> with <dim> uses the list form %s in its <name> (e.g. TIMER%s). svdconv supports dim peripherals only as arrays with [%s] at the end of the name, and drops the peripheral.
fix: Use the array form, e.g. <name>TIMER[%s]</name> with <dim> and <dimIncrement> (peripherals take no <dimIndex>), or write each instance as its own <peripheral>, using derivedFrom to share the registers.

cause: An element has <dim>1</dim>, so the array or list has a single instance.
fix: If there is only one instance, remove <dim>, <dimIncrement> and the %s / [%s] placeholder; otherwise set <dim> to the real number of instances.

cause: A <name>, <description>, register <displayName> or enumerated-value name contains a character svdconv does not support: a byte outside printable ASCII 0x20..0x7E (UTF-8 letters such as ä or µ, ©, typographic quotes or dashes, non-breaking spaces; each byte is reported) or a double quote. HEX shows the byte; line breaks and tabs are accepted.
fix: Replace the character with plain ASCII (e.g. 'u' for µ, ' instead of typographic quotes, - instead of an en dash) and remove double quotes from the text.
note: The text is kept unchanged in the model; only the SFD generator later drops such bytes (M516).

cause: A <name>, <description> or register <displayName> contains a backslash followed by a character other than 'n' (e.g. \t, \r, \\ or a Windows path). Only \n is supported in SVD texts.
fix: Remove the backslash, use \n for a line break, and write paths with '/'.

cause: The input file's extension is not .svd (case is ignored), e.g. .xml. svdconv takes the text after the last '.' of the full path, so an extensionless file inside a directory with a '.' in its name is reported here too.
fix: Rename the input file to <device name>.svd, matching <device><name>.

cause: Meant for an input file name without extension. In svdconv 30f5e81 it cannot appear: with no '.' anywhere in the absolute path svdconv aborts with a critical M104 exception, and with a '.' in a directory name it reports M221 instead.
fix: Rename the input file to <device name>.svd.
note: Bug: inputFileName.substr(pos) with pos == npos (SvdDevice.cpp:929) throws std::out_of_range before the M222 test runs.

cause: The SVD file name without path and extension differs from <device><name>; the comparison is case-sensitive (e.g. stm32f4.svd for <name>STM32F4</name>).
fix: Rename the file to exactly <device><name> plus .svd, or change <device><name> to match the file; the generated header is named after <device><name>.
note: Error under --strict.

cause: An <access> value uses the deprecated token read or write. svdconv maps it to read-only or write-only.
fix: Write <access>read-only</access> instead of read and <access>write-only</access> instead of write.

cause: A token value has the right letters but the wrong case, e.g. <access>Read-Write</access>, <usage>Registers</usage>, <endian>Little</endian>, <modifiedWriteValues>OneToClear</modifiedWriteValues> or <protection>S</protection>. svdconv accepts the value with a warning, except for <protection> and SAU values, which it also rejects with M202.
fix: Use the exact spelling shown as NAME2, which is the CMSIS-SVD.xsd token, e.g. read-write, registers, little, oneToClear, s/n/p.
note: Error under --strict.

cause: A <peripheral>, <cluster> or <register> contains more than one <dimArrayIndex>; only the first is used and the others are ignored.
fix: Keep one <dimArrayIndex> per array and put all its <enumeratedValue> entries into it.
note: Logged without a line number.

cause: A <register>, <cluster> or <peripheral> has <dimArrayIndex> but is not an array: it has no <dim>, or its <name> does not end with [%s]. The text always says 'Register', and NAME is the name of the <dimArrayIndex> container (often empty), not of the element.
fix: Make the element an array (<name>X[%s]</name> with <dim> and <dimIncrement>) or remove the <dimArrayIndex>.
note: For peripherals and clusters M242 or M243 is reported as well.

cause: An <enumeratedValue> in <dimArrayIndex> has a <value> that is not a valid array index: it is greater than or equal to <dim>. svdconv drops that enumeratedValue.
fix: Use values from 0 to dim-1 in <dimArrayIndex>, or raise <dim> if the array has more elements.

cause: An <enumeratedValue> inside <dimArrayIndex> uses <isDefault>. Each array index needs its own explicit <value>, so svdconv drops that enumeratedValue.
fix: Replace the <isDefault>true</isDefault> entry with one <enumeratedValue> per array index, each with an explicit <value>.

cause: A <peripheral> or <cluster> has a <headerStructName> that contains '%' (e.g. copied from a %s or [%s] name). svdconv ignores the headerStructName.
fix: Use a plain C identifier in <headerStructName>, e.g. <headerStructName>TIMER</headerStructName>, without %s or [%s].

cause: An <access> value is not one of read-only, write-only, read-write, writeOnce or read-writeOnce (or the deprecated read/write). svdconv treats the access as not set on that element; this is the <access> form of M202.
fix: Use one of the schema tokens in exact spelling, e.g. <access>read-write</access>.
note: Error under --strict.

cause: After the checks, a <peripheral> or a <cluster> directly inside a peripheral has no valid register left, because all its registers and clusters were dropped by earlier errors. svdconv then ignores the whole peripheral or cluster.
fix: Fix the errors reported earlier for the registers and clusters inside it; the message goes away once at least one register is valid.
note: Error under --strict. A peripheral with no registers at all gets M328 instead.

cause: A <field> has <dim> and a <name> ending in [%s]. Fields cannot be arrays, so svdconv drops the field.
fix: Use the list form with %s, e.g. <name>EN%s</name> with <dim>, <dimIncrement> as the bit distance and optionally <dimIndex>, which creates fields EN0, EN1, ...

cause: A <dimName> contains %s. <dimName> is the type name generated for a dim cluster and must be a plain identifier, so svdconv drops the element.
fix: Remove %s from <dimName>, e.g. <dimName>CHANNEL</dimName>.

cause: A <cluster> named just %s (a nameless dim cluster whose instances are named by <dimIndex>) has no <dimName>. svdconv needs <dimName> as the generated type name and drops the cluster.
fix: Add <dimName> to the cluster, e.g. <name>%s</name><dim>2</dim><dimIncrement>0x10</dimIncrement><dimIndex>TX,RX</dimIndex><dimName>CHANNEL</dimName>, or give the cluster a real name such as CH%s.

note: Not raised anywhere in svdconv at 30f5e81: the code appears only in the message table (SVDConv_Msgs.cpp:105) and the README (README.md:284).

cause: An element has <dim> but its <name> contains no placeholder: neither %s nor [%s] at the end. svdconv cannot name the instances and drops the element; a [%s] that is not at the end of the name is not recognised and also lands here.
fix: Add the placeholder: [%s] at the end for an array (REG[%s]) or %s for a list (CH%s_CTRL); otherwise remove <dim> and <dimIncrement>.
note: Error under --strict.

cause: A dim element (any tag whose name contains 'dim') is not accepted on this level by svdconv: <dimIndex> or <dimName> on a <peripheral>, <dimName> on a <register>, <dimArrayIndex> on a <field>, or any dim element on an <interrupt>. Misspelled tags containing 'dim' land here too. svdconv drops the parent element.
fix: Remove the element or move it to a level that takes it: peripherals take <dim>, <dimIncrement>, <dimArrayIndex>; clusters also <dimIndex> and <dimName>; registers <dim>, <dimIncrement>, <dimIndex>, <dimArrayIndex>; fields <dim>, <dimIncrement>, <dimIndex>, <dimName>. Check the tag spelling.

cause: Meant for a dim element whose <name>, <displayName> or <description> has [%s] somewhere other than at the end. In svdconv 30f5e81 the expression parser never returns that result, so such a name surfaces as M239 instead.
fix: Put [%s] at the very end of the name (REG[%s]), or use %s for a list.
note: Unreachable at 30f5e81: ARRAYINVALID is commented out in SvdUtils::ParseExpression (SvdUtils.cpp:140).

cause: A <peripheral> or <cluster> has <dimArrayIndex> but no <dim>; svdconv also reports M229.
fix: Make it an array with <dim>, <dimIncrement> and a <name> ending in [%s], or remove the <dimArrayIndex>.

cause: A <peripheral> or <cluster> has <dim> and <dimArrayIndex>, but its <name> uses %s instead of ending with [%s], so it is not an array; svdconv also reports M229.
fix: End the <name> with [%s] (e.g. UART[%s]) or remove the <dimArrayIndex>.
